neurological_exam.motor: Left hand: intrinsic 3/5, thenar atrophy prominent. Right hand: intrinsic 4/5. Bilateral arm weakness deltoids 4/5. Right leg: tibialis anterior 4+/5. Left leg: 5/5. Visible fasciculations bilateral deltoids and calves.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 3+, brachioradialis 3+ bilaterally. Knee jerks 3+. Ankle jerks 2+. Hoffman bilateral. Babinski right.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive left hand weakness and wasting over 12 months, then right leg weakness
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. G is a 58-year-old right-handed accountant with a 12-month history of progressive left hand weakness and wasting, followed 5 months ago by right leg weakness and bilateral fasciculations. He initially noticed difficulty with fine motor tasks using his left hand — shuffling papers, manipulating a stapler. He observed progressive wasting of his left hand intrinsic muscles. Over the past 5 months, he developed right foot dragging and right calf wasting. He has noticed twitching in both arms and legs at rest. His wife observed tongue twitching. He denies sensory symptoms, swallowing difficulties, or speech changes. Examination confirms combined UMN and LMN signs in a classic distribution. This is a textbook straightforward ALS presentation that an intern should identify correctly.

findings.location: Bilateral corticospinal tracts, posterior limb internal capsule

mri.impression: 1. Bilateral symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity of the corticospinal tracts, including posterior limb of internal capsule. 2. Low T2 signal band at the bilateral primary motor cortex. No mass, hemorrhage, or demyelinating lesions. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Tongue: fibrillations +2, fasciculation potentials (complex). Reduced recruitment.

Left FDI, APB, biceps, triceps: fibrillations +2-3, complex fasciculations, large amplitude long duration polyphasic MUPs, severely reduced recruitment. Right FDI: fibrillations +1. Cervical paraspinals bilateral: fibrillations +1.
Right TA: fibrillations +2, fasciculations, large MUPs. Left TA: fibrillations +1. Bilateral gastrocnemii: fasciculations.
All sensory NCS normal bilaterally — critical finding.
Reduced CMAP amplitudes. Normal conduction velocities. No conduction block.

specialized_test.impression: Active denervation (fibrillations, fasciculation potentials) and chronic reinnervation changes (large amplitude polyphasic MUPs, reduced recruitment) in bulbar, cervical, thoracic, and lumbosacral regions — four body regions involved. Sensory NCS normal bilaterally. Reduced CMAP amplitudes; normal conduction velocities; no conduction block. Findings indicate a widespread disorder of lower anterior horn cells. Clinical correlation required.
